title: Implement beginner-facing documentation and reference updates
scope: Edit top-level beginner-facing documentation and references after hook and skill edits are available for linking. Do not redo T009/T010 edits unless a small consistency fix is unavoidable; record such fixes explicitly.

Update README.md so it distinguishes beginner materials from advanced/local examples, accounts for the actual skills and hooks present in the repo, and uses README.md files as acceptable homes for setup instructions.

Update recommendations.md while preserving the high-level path: try chat tools, try one agentic tool on a real project, learn permissions, manage context. Add the local-vs-general distinction and avoid making advanced hooks, aliases, or high-privilege profiles sound like defaults.

In recommendations.md, incorporate the user's current decisions: the tmux/Pi orchestration skill can be provided as one method among many; native subagent workflows should be mentioned where verified; agents can help port/adapt the skill or task pattern to preferred tools; agent-assisted installation/customization is preferred over blind scripts or manual copy-paste.

Verify, cite, or soften volatile claims in recommendations.md: paid tiers/pricing, response-time ranges, /init availability, sandboxing and auto-mode behavior, context-size degradation around 100-150k tokens, and permission-fatigue claims.

Update references.md only for concrete needs discovered in T008 or this task. Add official documentation for retained capability/configuration claims and primary or peer-reviewed sources for retained human-behavior cautionary claims. Verify DOI/arXiv/figure details before changing existing entries.

Inspect ai-tools-guide.md and ai-tools-onepager.md only if the edits introduce claims that must be synchronized with them, or if T008/T007 identifies a likely mismatch. If they are not edited, state why in the handoff.
goals: Update /home/abhmul/Documents/ai-tools-intro/references.md only if needed for retained claims.
non_goals: Do not edit reports/generalization-review.md or reports/generalization-review-presentation.html unless creating an erratum task instead.
Do not introduce new hard-coded model version names except specific examples or verified product-version caveats already needed for Codex config.
Do not read private shell configuration.
safety: Audience is newcomers with no AI experience; use plain language and define terms.
Tone must be neutral and factual; no hype, slogans, or emoji.
Capability claims must trace to official documentation; cautionary claims must come from primary or peer-reviewed sources in references.md, not inline.
Keep guide and one-pager in sync where applicable.
Do not use Python unless you first read /home/abhmul/Documents/vaults/agent-vault/agent-python/README or README.md if present.
success_criteria: README.md accurately frames beginner materials versus advanced/local examples and links the relevant README.md or skill files.
recommendations.md no longer presents advanced hooks/aliases/high-privilege auto profiles as beginner defaults.
All retained capability/configuration claims have official-source traceability via references.md, inline links, or T008-backed source links as appropriate to the file.
Human-behavior cautions are either supported in references.md by primary/peer-reviewed sources or softened into personal workflow advice.
Handoff lists changed files, source-backed claims used, claims softened/removed, and any guide/one-pager sync decision.
